question.text: Will Mexican federal authorities have confirmed recovery of all nine radioactive packages stolen in the November 7, 2026 Tlaxcala truck crash by November 27, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, by the end of November 27, 2026 (Mexico City time, UTC−6), Mexican federal authorities have publicly confirmed that all nine packages of radioactive material looted from the crashed ININ (Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Nucleares) transport vehicle on the Huamantla–Tlaxcala highway in Tlaxcala, Mexico, on November 7, 2026 have been located and secured, or that all of the radioactive material those nine packages contained has been located and secured. Confirmations made in separate statements count cumulatively, and an unqualified federal statement that the stolen radioactive material has been recovered counts as YES unless it indicates that one or more packages or items remain missing. Qualifying statements may come from any Mexican federal government body, including the Presidency, SENER, SSPC, SEGOB/CNPC, CNSNS, ININ, FGR and the Guardia Nacional, and must be reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions); official communiqués are published at https://www.gob.mx/cnsns and https://www.gob.mx/sspc, and running coverage of the case is compiled at https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2026/11/10/se-mantiene-alerta-en-siete-estados-por-robo-de-material-radiactivo-tras-volcadura-de-vehiculo-oficial-en-tlaxcala/. If no such confirmation has been published by that time — including if authorities confirm only some of the packages or only some of the material as recovered — the question resolves NO.
question.fine_print: If authorities officially revise the number of packages that were stolen, the question resolves YES only once every package in the revised official count has been located and secured (or all of the radioactive material they contained has been). Finding containers that are empty or damaged counts only if authorities also state that the radioactive material itself has been located and secured. Statements that the material's radioactivity has decayed, or that it no longer poses a health risk, do not count as confirmation of recovery. Announcements by state or municipal officials (for example, the governors of Tlaxcala or Veracruz) do not by themselves satisfy the criterion unless a Mexican federal authority confirms them.

research:
I found no confirmation that any of the nine packages has been recovered, let alone all nine. The newest report on the case is from 2026-11-13, and nothing settles the question yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The Infobae running-coverage page named in the criteria loads, but it holds only the original alert story and background on past theft cases. It reports no recovery and the alert is still active. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2026/11/10/se-mantiene-alerta-en-siete-estados-por-robo-de-material-radiactivo-tras-volcadura-de-vehiculo-oficial-en-tlaxcala/)
- 2026-11-16: The CNSNS press archive feed only returned a 2019 item, so it doesn't seem to be kept up to date. I found no 2026 CNSNS communiqué there. [gob.mx/cnsns](https://www.gob.mx/cnsns/es/archivo/prensa)
- I could not find any CNSNS, CNPC, SSPC or FGR communiqué announcing a recovery, or any federal bulletin about the case dated after the initial alert.

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. Nothing I found says any of the nine boxes has been located. The seven-state alert was still in force as of 2026-11-13.
- One sign that leans the other way: a Tlaxcala state official said the case would be **reclassified as theft of medical material**, and that federal authorities will decide whether to lift the alert. Under the fine print, lifting or downgrading the alert without stating the material was recovered would not count as YES.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: Antonio Martínez Velázquez, Tlaxcala's state communications coordinator (CCOM), said the FGR found the material was for medical use, "perhaps for cancer." He said the alert "will be reclassified as theft of medical material" and that federal authorities will decide whether to remove it. He mentioned inconsistencies in the timeline, in how the boxes were taken and in the chain of custody. No recovery was reported. [Periódico Enfoque](https://www.periodicoenfoque.com.mx/tlaxcala/fgr-confirma-que-material-robado-en-tlaxcala-era-de-uso-medico)
- 2026-11-12: Satirical and other national coverage. No recovery. [El Deforma](https://eldeforma.com/2026/11/12/tlaxcala-rapina-camion-material-radiactivo/)
- 2026-11-11: According to the same official, the FGR identified a probable culprit and was expected to announce procedural steps "in the coming hours." I found no follow-up announcement. The Navy (Secretaría de Marina) issued an operational directive to coordinate federal and state forces in the search. The containers had "not yet been recovered." [Intolerancia Diario](https://intoleranciadiario.com/tlax/articles/2026/11/11/1060317-robo-de-material-radiactivo-en-tlaxcala-con-muchas-inconsistencias-fgr-tendria-identificado-a-presunto-responsable.html), [Síntesis](https://sintesis.mx/2026/11/11/fgr-responsable-robo-de-material-radiactivo/), [Gentetlx](https://gentetlx.com.mx/2026/11/11/identifican-a-probable-responsable-del-robo-de-material-radiactivo-en-tlaxcala/)
- 2026-11-11: Federal and state forces were inspecting roads and scrap/collection centres in the seven states. [El Imparcial](https://www.elimparcial.com/mexico/2026/11/11/esto-se-sabe-de-la-alerta-por-material-radioactivo-robado-en-tlaxcala-y-que-mantiene-en-riesgo-a-varios-estados/)
- 2026-11-09: Veracruz Governor Rocío Nahle: the material "was lost in the Tlaxcala area" and had not been recovered. [El Portavoz](https://elportavoz.com.mx/aun-no-se-localiza-contenedor-con-material-radiactivo/)
- 2026-11-08/09: CNPC/CNSNS issued the alert for nine boxes (Tc-99m ×3, I-131 ×4, Tl ×1, Sm ×1), IAEA Category 4, with no sign of a leak at the crash site. [Milenio](https://www.milenio.com/estados/roban-material-radiactivo-tlaxcala-rapina-emiten-alerta), [UnoTV](https://www.unotv.com/nacional/roban-material-radiactivo-de-uso-medico-en-tlaxcala-emiten-alerta-en-siete-estados/)
- The news-API articles supplied with the question (2026-11-13 to 11-15) are about unrelated crashes and robberies. None mentions this case.

## 4. Base rates
- Past cases compiled by Infobae: thefts in Ciudad Obregón and Calpulalpan, Tlaxcala (2020), recovered; Teoloyucan/Tecámac (April 2021), source found abandoned one day later; Edomex radiography device (September 2022), recovered two days later; Salamanca and Tabasco Ir-192 thefts, recovered. Two 2019 Cs-137 cases (Michoacán, Matamoros) were recorded as losses. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2026/11/10/se-mantiene-alerta-en-siete-estados-por-robo-de-material-radiactivo-tras-volcadura-de-vehiculo-oficial-en-tlaxcala/)
- CNSNS figures for 2018: 12 of 14 theft cases ended in recovery (from the question background; I did not verify this).
- How this case differs:
  - Nine separate boxes taken by a crowd during looting, not one device taken by one thief, so recovering all nine is a stricter test than a typical case.
  - Most past recoveries happened within about 1 to 7 days. This case is now at day 9 with nothing found.
  - Officials are already talking down the radiological framing, through the reclassification remark and the low-risk category.
- One search summary mentioned a past episode in which the material was never recovered and CNSNS considered its short half-life made it no radiological risk. I could not tell which case that was.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the pre-fetched Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question; they cover Tlaxcala elections, GTA VI and similar. I found no Metaculus, Manifold or expert forecast on this case.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2026-11-27
- A possible FGR arrest or search warrant against the identified suspect. That could lead to some or all boxes being turned in, but it was flagged on 11-11 and nothing has followed so far.
- A possible federal decision to lift or downgrade the CNPC alert. That would be NO-relevant unless it says the material was recovered.
- Possible discovery by scrap dealers or residents, or boxes being handed in voluntarily.
- President Sheinbaum's daily press conferences (mañaneras) and CNSNS/CNPC bulletins. I found no mention of the case at a mañanera so far.

Sources: the links given inline above.

## 4. Base rates
- 2017-06-30 (the closest past case): A courier van carrying short-lived medical radioactive material was stolen in Guadalajara. The material was **never recovered**. CNSNS said its low activity and short half-life meant it posed no radiological risk. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2026/11/10/se-mantiene-alerta-en-siete-estados-por-robo-de-material-radiactivo-tras-volcadura-de-vehiculo-oficial-en-tlaxcala/)
- Recovered cases, almost all single sealed industrial or medical sources:
  - 2013 Co-60, recovered after 2 days
  - 2018-07 Ir-192 in Mexico City, recovered after 8 days through an anonymous tip
  - 2021-04 Ir-192 from Teoloyucan, recovered after 1 day
  - 2022-09 Ir-192 in Estado de México, recovered after 2 days
  - Cases in Calpulalpan, Tlaxcala (2020) and Ciudad Obregón (2020), both recovered [same source]
- Recoveries usually come within days. This case is already 9 days old without one. It also requires all nine boxes, and they were looted by several people during a rapiña (crowd looting after the crash), not taken as one source.
- The question background also cites a CNSNS figure of 12 recoveries out of 14 thefts in 2018. I did not verify that number.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied (Tlaxcala elections, Sheinbaum, GTA VI and others) relate to this question. I found no prediction market or expert forecast on whether the material will be recovered.

## 6. Upcoming events before November 27
- The FGR could announce the arrest of the identified suspect, which might come with a recovery.
- The federal government could formally reclassify or lift the alert (Tlaxcala says that is a federal decision). Lifting it without a recovery statement would not count as YES.
- A CNSNS, CNPC or SSPC bulletin, or a mention at Sheinbaum's daily press conference (the mañanera), would be the likely channel for any confirmation.
- Decay: by about November 27, the Mo-99 will be down to roughly 0.3% of its starting activity and the I-131 to roughly 20%. Statements about decay or low risk do not count toward resolution.

Note: the news-API articles supplied (crashes, robberies and other cases from November 13 to 15) have nothing to do with this question.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 11 days remain, until November 27, 2026 at 23:59 Mexico City time. For YES, a Mexican federal body (CNSNS, CNPC, FGR, SSPC, the Presidency or similar) must publicly confirm, in one statement or several, that all nine looted packages, or all of the radioactive material in them, have been located and secured. An unqualified federal statement that "the material was recovered" would also count.

(b) Status quo: nothing has been recovered as of day 9, coverage has gone quiet since November 13, and officials are downgrading the case to "theft of medical material." If nothing changes, the answer is NO.

(c) Base rate:
- Mexican radioactive-source thefts end in recovery about 80 to 85% of the time, but nearly all of those cases involve a single sealed source, usually recovered within 1 to 8 days.
- The closest analogue is the 2017 Guadalajara theft of short-lived medical isotopes. That material was never recovered, and CNSNS dismissed the risk because of decay.
- Conditioning on no recovery by day 9, with nine items scattered by crowd looting, and requiring all nine within the window, I put the base rate at roughly 10 to 15%.

(d) Evidence:
- For YES: the FGR identified a probable responsible person (November 11-12) and cited "inconsistencies" in the timeline, the extraction and the chain of custody. That could mean an insider, or a single actor holding all the boxes, so one arrest could recover everything at once. SEMAR, federal forces and scrap-yard inspections were active (November 11).
- For NO: no recovery by November 9-13, no follow-up from the FGR after promising announcements "in the coming hours," and the reclassification remark on November 13, with the alert possibly lifted without a recovery. Falling radioactivity removes the urgency. The YES bar is strict: all nine packages, confirmed by a federal body.

(e) NO scenario: the alert is quietly lifted or downgraded as the isotopes decay. Perhaps a few boxes turn up, or an arrest is announced, but no federal statement says all nine were secured.
YES scenario: the FGR arrests the suspect, who turns out to have taken the boxes as a group, and the FGR or CNSNS announces that the nine containers were recovered and handed to ININ.

(f) I start near 12% from the conditional base rate. The suspect lead and the "inconsistencies" pointing to a single actor push up slightly. The de-escalation, the silence since November 13 and the all-nine requirement push down. I land at about 10%.

Probability: 10%

(a) About 11.5 days remain, until the end of November 27, 2026 (Mexico City time). For YES, a Mexican federal body (CNSNS, CNPC, FGR, SSPC, SEMAR or similar) must publicly confirm that all nine boxes, or all of the radioactive material in them, have been located and secured. Credible media must report the confirmation. Partial recoveries, alert downgrades and "no longer risky" statements do not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the question resolves NO. As of day 9 there is no confirmed recovery of any box, and coverage effectively stopped after November 13.

(c) Base rate: single-source thefts in Mexico are usually recovered, roughly 80-85% (12 of 14 in 2018), and typically within 1 to 8 days. This case belongs to a narrower class: short-lived medical material, multiple items taken by a crowd, and nothing found after a week or more. Recovery in that class is much rarer. The closest precedent, the 2017 Guadalajara courier theft of short-lived medical material, was never recovered. Conditional on no recovery by day 9 and on needing all nine items, I put the base rate at roughly 10-15%.

(d) Evidence:
- For YES:
  - On November 11-12 the FGR said it had identified a probable responsible person.
  - Officials cited "inconsistencies" in the timeline, in how the boxes were taken and in the chain of custody. This hints at an insider or single actor who might hold all the boxes together.
  - On November 11, SEMAR and other forces were searching roads and scrap yards across the seven states.
- For NO:
  - No recovery has been reported through November 16.
  - The FGR's promised follow-up "in coming hours" (November 11) never came.
  - On November 13, Tlaxcala's CCOM said the case would be reclassified as theft of medical material and that federal authorities would decide whether to lift the alert, a sign of de-escalation.
  - The material decays fast (Mo-99 below 1% by November 27), so the incentive to keep searching falls.
  - All nine boxes are required, and they were dispersed among looters.

(e) Scenarios:
- NO: The alert is quietly lifted or downgraded around November 20, with CNSNS noting the material has decayed and poses no risk. Some boxes may turn up, but there is no federal statement that all nine are secured.
- YES: The FGR executes a search warrant on the identified suspect, who turns out to be connected to the transport. All nine boxes are found together, and CNSNS or the FGR announces that the material is secured.

(f) Starting from roughly 12%, I move down slightly. Officials are de-escalating, the promised FGR follow-up never came, and requiring every box is a strict test. The insider-suspect angle stops me going lower, since it is the main route to finding all nine boxes in one place. No market covers this question.

Probability: 8%

(a) About 11.5 days remain, until the end of November 27, 2026 (Mexico City time). For Yes, a Mexican federal body (CNSNS, CNPC, FGR, SSPC, ININ, the Presidency and so on) must publicly confirm that all nine looted packages, or all of their radioactive material, have been located and secured. An unqualified federal statement that the stolen material was recovered also counts. Statements about decay or low risk do not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of November 13 to 16, none of the nine boxes had been reported located, and coverage has gone quiet.

(c) Base rate: Mexican radioactive-source thefts usually end in recovery. CNSNS recorded 12 of 14 in 2018, roughly 80 to 85%, and most recoveries came within 1 to 8 days. That reference class is mostly single sealed industrial sources with clear value or salience. Three things cut it sharply for this case:
- The closest analogue, the 2017 Guadalajara theft of short-lived medical isotopes, was never recovered.
